primary.priority: Use this deck for slide size, header/footer geometry, page-number location, typography scale, color identity, figure scale, and visual rhythm.

secondary.priority: Use this deck for research-story pacing, progressive disclosure, model/process explanation, result presentation, and Summary & Future Work structure. Do not convert new slides to 4:3.

reference_asset_policy.rule: Images, scientific diagrams, data, citations, equations, and subject-matter content inside the reference decks are reference material for layout/style analysis only. Never reuse them in a new presentation unless the user explicitly provides the same asset as source content for the new topic.
prohibited: copy ENIAC, IBM, quantum-computing, MTJ, MRAM, or other reference-deck scientific images into an unrelated presentation
copy reference-deck numerical data into an unrelated presentation
copy reference-deck citations into an unrelated presentation
use reference-deck screenshots as background decoration

output_scope.cover_rule: Do not create a title/cover slide.
output_scope.page_count_rule: The user-requested slide count means generated content slides only.

slide_numbering.rule: Because no cover slide is generated, Outline must display page number 1.

template_mode.rule: If the laboratory PowerPoint template/reference deck is available during final PPTX assembly, use its existing 16:9 content-slide layout as the base. Preserve the master/layout and replace only editable title/content/citation areas.
do_not: replace the laboratory shell with a generic modern theme
convert the deck into card-based or dashboard-style slides
treat reference scientific images as template assets

fallback_if_template_file_unavailable.rule: Reproduce only the measured fixed geometric identity described in this JSON. Do not invent missing logos or branding artwork; reserve their positions instead.
fallback_if_template_file_unavailable.branding_asset_behavior: Use only actual user-provided branding assets.

slide_size.rule: Always use the 2020 reference deck's 16:9 canvas. The 2018 4:3 deck is not a canvas-size reference.

title_zone.rule: Large left-aligned title at the top. Prefer one line.

top_separator.rule: Treat as fixed laboratory identity. Do not use this separator as a content graphic.

main_content_zone.rule: Scientific content stays between the top separator and citation area.

citation_zone.rule: Use only when the slide has a user-provided/source-supported citation. Keep clear of the footer and page number.

footer.rule: Footer is fixed template identity and must never be covered by research content.

page_number.rule: Show on every generated content slide. Outline is 1.

rules: Black is the default content color.
Blue is used for key numerical results, positive emphasis, important scientific terms, or the emphasized branch of a comparison.
Red is reserved for warnings, limitations, contradictory trends, or critical contrast.
Yellow primarily belongs to the laboratory template identity; use it sparingly inside content.
Do not introduce a new decorative color palette.

title.rule: Prefer a single-line title. Shorten the title before reducing below 40 pt.

body.rule: Use phrases and labels rather than paragraphs.

figure_label.weight: Bold when it functions as a category or comparison label

typography.hierarchy_rule: If the content does not fit at these sizes, split the slide. Never shrink text to force dense content.

section_outline_repetition.rule: The reference decks sometimes repeat Outline slides as section markers, but new short presentations should not spend extra slides on repeated Outline pages unless the user explicitly requests them or the deck is long enough to benefit.

presentation_structure.rule: Build a clear research narrative rather than a sequence of text summaries.

core_characteristics: processes shown with arrows and repeated stages
little decorative chrome inside the content area

representative_patterns.timeline: Three or more stages arranged left-to-right with images, stage labels, dates/parameters, and one dominant arrow.
representative_patterns.image_text: One large figure occupies roughly half to two-thirds of the content area; the remaining space contains only the few labels or callouts necessary to explain it.
representative_patterns.comparison: Two or three aligned visual columns with matched image sizes and concise labels.
representative_patterns.mechanism: Scientific diagram centered or dominant, with short labels and arrows that explain direction or causality.
representative_patterns.process_flow: A repeated flow structure is carried across consecutive slides, revealing one new stage at a time.
representative_patterns.experimental_result: Graph or measurement figure is dominant; 2-4 concise callouts identify trend, parameter, or conclusion.
representative_patterns.application_map: One central concept connected spatially to a small number of application branches with representative figures.
representative_patterns.summary_future: Connect achieved result -> extracted insight -> next application/future work using a visual flow, not a paragraph list.

selection_rules.background_or_motivation: Prefer one large concept image/diagram plus 2-4 concise labels.
selection_rules.method: Prefer process-flow, architecture, device schematic, or staged experimental sequence.
selection_rules.comparison: Use aligned side-by-side columns with equal visual weight.
selection_rules.result: Make the source figure the main object; add only trend/parameter callouts supported by the source.
selection_rules.multiple_results: Split across consecutive slides instead of making one dashboard.
selection_rules.formula_or_model: Show the formula/model independently with variable labels and one adjacent physical interpretation figure when available.
selection_rules.future_work: Use one direction per branch or one future direction per slide if explanation is substantial.

content_density.preferred_visible_text: short phrases, labels, equations, parameters, and figure annotations
content_density.rule: Do not convert scientific content into a long prose summary. Visual evidence should carry the slide whenever source figures exist.

image_rules.source_policy: Use only images supplied by the user or explicitly contained in the user's source documents for the new presentation.
image_rules.filename_policy: When source image filenames are available, preserve the exact filenames in the generated slide specification.
image_rules.two_images: Align side-by-side with matched height unless their scientific aspect ratios require otherwise.
image_rules.three_images: Use three columns or one-main-two-supporting structure.
image_rules.four_images: Use 2x2 only when all four figures are equally important.
avoid: decorative image crops that remove scientific context
reusing images from the reference decks solely because they look good
image_rules.shadow: Subtle figure shadow is allowed only when it matches the reference slide and does not reduce scientific clarity.

data.rule: Use only numbers explicitly provided by the user or source documents.

formula.rule: Preserve symbols, subscripts, superscripts, units, and variable names exactly. Do not invent missing equations.

citation.rule: Cite only sources explicitly provided by the user/source documents. Keep citations directly relevant to the current slide.

outline_slide.title: Outline
outline_slide.goal: Show the research story at a glance.
preferred_layouts: major-section labels with a representative source figure preview if available
avoid: more than one sentence per section

purpose: explain what the audience should observe in the figure
connect the visual evidence to the conclusion
provide a short transition when useful
speaker_notes.accuracy_rule: Speaker notes must obey the same no-hallucination rule as visible slide content.

prohibited: copy unrelated content from the reference decks

checks: Slide 1 is Outline and displays page number 1.
All subsequent content slides have sequential page numbers.
Slide size is 16:9 at 13.333 x 7.5 inches.
Top separator and bottom NanoSTLab footer are preserved and unobstructed.
Reference-deck scientific images are not reused unless explicitly supplied as new-topic source assets.
Every slide communicates one main message.
Figures dominate over prose whenever source figures exist.
No body text is smaller than 21 pt unless it is a caption or citation.
Citations remain approximately 10 pt and above the footer.
No image is stretched and no axes, legends, units, or scale bars are hidden.
No unsupported data, formulas, citations, or conclusions are introduced.
There are no UI cards, dashboard layouts, excessive rounded boxes, or unrelated icons.
The deck visually resembles NanoSTLab academic presentations through hierarchy, figure use, flow, color emphasis, and spacing—not by copying unrelated scientific content.
quality_control.failure_action: If a slide fails any check, revise the layout or split the content. Do not solve the problem by shrinking text or removing scientific context.

prompt_generation_priority: 2. No-cover structure with Outline as Slide 1
5. One main scientific message per slide
